reading.stem: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks:
Dear Shop Owners,
Our student council is organizing a town history quiz in May. Families have offered to set up tables, and the hall has already been booked. We hope to give the winning team prizes from neighborhood businesses so that students also get to know the shops around them. Would your business be willing to donate a small item or a gift certificate for one of the prizes? A book, a plant, or a voucher for a snack would all be welcome. We will thank contributing shops in the program.
Sincerely, Mira, Student Council Chair
choices: 퀴즈 대회의 상품으로 사용할 물품이나 상품권을 후원받으려고
동네 상점 주인에게 심사 위원을 맡기려고
우승 팀의 상점 견학 날짜를 결정하려고
evidence: Would your business be willing to donate a small item or a gift certificate for one of the prizes?
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 글의 목적
장소와 운영 인력은 이미 확보했다. 편지의 구체적인 요청은 우승 팀에게 줄 상품의 기부이다.
근거 “Would your business be willing to donate a small item or a gift certificate for one of the prizes?”

reading.stem: 다음 글에 드러난 주인공의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: Joon was adjusting the projector when a message appeared: his partner's train had stopped between stations. The presentation was due to begin in two minutes, and the first half of their slides belonged to her. He could hear his own breath above the projector fan. Then he remembered that each had rehearsed the other's section in case of trouble. He began with the photograph they had discussed the night before. One slide led naturally to the next. When the class applauded the final slide, he let out the breath he seemed to have held throughout the talk.
evidence: When the class applauded the final slide, he let out the breath he seemed to have held throughout the talk.
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 심경 변화
발표 직전 동료가 오지 못해 긴장하지만, 혼자 끝까지 발표하고 박수를 듣자 긴장이 풀린다.
근거 “When the class applauded the final slide, he let out the breath he seemed to have held throughout the talk.”

reading.stem: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: Two volunteers can give the same public tour and receive quite different marks if no one agrees what a successful tour is. One judge may count the facts mentioned; another may reward questions from visitors. Showing the volunteers their scores afterwards does not repair the disagreement. Before the tours begin, the organization should decide what matters and share examples of the performance it expects. The judges will then have a common reference, and the volunteers can direct their practice toward a visible goal. Make the criteria clear to the people doing the work before using those criteria to judge them.
choices: 평가 전에 업무 담당자와 평가 기준을 명확하게 공유해야 한다.
봉사자의 연습은 점수를 공개한 뒤부터 시작해야 한다.
서로 다른 평가 결과는 하나의 점수로 평균 내면 충분하다.
심사 위원 수를 줄이면 평가 기준을 정할 필요가 없다.
관람객의 질문 수만으로 안내의 질을 평가해야 한다.
evidence: Make the criteria clear to the people doing the work before using those criteria to judge them.
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 필자의 주장
점수를 사후에 공개해도 심사 기준의 불일치는 해결되지 않는다. 기준을 미리 정하고 당사자가 이해하도록 공유하라는 주장이다.
근거 “Make the criteria clear to the people doing the work before using those criteria to judge them.”

reading.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>give the steepest hill the freshest legs</u>의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
blocks: My colleague likes to <u>give the steepest hill the freshest legs</u>. There is no hill on her way to the office. What she means becomes clear when we look at her calendar. The budget calculations occupy the hour in which she is usually most alert. Routine orders wait until the quiet dip after lunch. For another colleague the order is reversed, because he thinks more clearly late in the day. The practice is not a rule about breakfast or about getting up early. It is a decision to match the hardest work to the period when one's attention is strongest.
choices: divide every assignment into equally long pieces
reserve one's highest-energy period for demanding tasks
delay routine duties until a colleague volunteers
put urgent requests ahead of difficult tasks every morning
complete all physical exercise before starting office work
evidence: It is a decision to match the hardest work to the period when one's attention is strongest.
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 함축 의미
가파른 언덕과 생생한 다리는 어려운 업무와 높은 집중력에 해당한다. 집중이 잘되는 시간은 사람마다 다를 수 있다.
근거 “It is a decision to match the hardest work to the period when one's attention is strongest.”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: A person may put off learning the guitar for weeks, then take the first lesson on an otherwise ordinary Tuesday. What changed? Tuesday happened to be the first day in her new apartment. A date that marks a fresh chapter can draw a line between the person who postponed the lesson and the person who intends to begin. The instrument has not become easier to play. The psychological distance from past delays has simply made the first step more inviting. Treating a date as a new beginning can increase willingness to start working toward a goal.
choices: 목표를 세울 때는 생활 환경의 변화를 피하는 것이 낫다.
어려운 기술은 한 주의 첫날에만 제대로 익힐 수 있다.
날짜를 따로 정하면 준비할 시간이 부족해진다.
목표 달성에 실패한 기억은 새 장소에서 더 선명해진다.
어떤 날을 새 출발로 인식하면 목표에 착수하려는 마음이 강해질 수 있다.
evidence: Treating a date as a new beginning can increase willingness to start working toward a goal.
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 글의 요지
새집의 첫날은 악기 자체를 쉽게 만들지 않지만 과거의 미루기와 거리를 느끼게 해 행동을 시작할 계기가 된다.
근거 “Treating a date as a new beginning can increase willingness to start working toward a goal.”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: Before a rowing team leaves the dock, its members sometimes repeat a short chant. To an observer the words may sound unimportant; in fact, another set of words with the same beat could serve much the same purpose. Each voice gives the others a signal about when to breathe and move. A nervous newcomer can fall into step without receiving a separate instruction. The chant may also lift the crew's energy just when a demanding effort is about to begin. Shared rhythm helps transform several separate efforts into one coordinated group action.
choices: the role of group rhythm in preparing people to act together
the origins of different designs of racing boats
the advantage of individual training before joining a crew
the importance of using complicated words in a team chant
the development of written rules for rowing competitions
evidence: Shared rhythm helps transform several separate efforts into one coordinated group action.
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 글의 주제
구호의 단어 자체보다 박자를 맞추는 일이 호흡과 행동을 조율하고 집단의 활동을 준비시킨다는 글이다.
근거 “Shared rhythm helps transform several separate efforts into one coordinated group action.”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: A commuter can pedal to work in an old jacket, yet a cycling club's weekend ride may display an astonishing range of matching clothes and costly accessories. Some items improve comfort. Others do something less visible: they tell fellow riders what sort of cyclist the owner hopes to be. A repaired steel frame can carry that message as clearly as an expensive new one if the group values careful restoration. The meaning resides partly in the community that reads the object. Equipment chosen for a leisure activity can express membership and identity in addition to serving a practical purpose.
choices: The Health Benefits of Weekend Cycling
Why a Costly Bicycle Must Be Faster
How to Replace Clubs with Solo Rides
The Commuter's Guide to Mending a Jacket
What a Bicycle Says Before the Ride Begins
evidence: Equipment chosen for a leisure activity can express membership and identity in addition to serving a practical purpose.
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 글의 제목
장비는 주행을 돕는 물건이면서 집단 속에서 자신이 어떤 사람인지 나타내는 표시이기도 하다. 비싼 장비만이 그런 역할을 하는 것은 아니다.
근거 “Equipment chosen for a leisure activity can express membership and identity in addition to serving a practical purpose.”

reading.stem: 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

title: Completion of Two-Dose Vaccination Schedules
blocks.note: Case study data for this exercise.

blocks: Each bar gives the percentage of children in a fictional district who had completed both visits by the survey date.
choices: For North, the figure for Year 2 was below the figure for Year 1.
One of the two figures for West was below 30%, and the other was above it.
For Year 2, Central ranked lowest among the five categories.
For Year 1, the figure for East was lower than that for Central by 22 percentage points.
The two bars for South are 24 percentage points apart.
evidence: South: 67, 48
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 도표 내용 불일치
South의 두 값은 67%와 48%이므로 차이는 19%포인트이다.
[지문 근거] “South: 67, 48”

reading.stem: Janaki Ammal에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
blocks: Janaki Ammal chose higher education when her family expected her to marry. Botany took her from India to the United States, where the University of Michigan awarded her a doctorate. She studied sugarcane and later worked in Britain on a reference book about the chromosomes of cultivated plants. India called her home to help improve food production. That goal did not make her willing to accept every development scheme. In particular, she spoke out for the native plants of Silent Valley when construction threatened their habitat.
choices: 인도로 돌아온 뒤에야 처음으로 영국에서 염색체 책 작업을 했다.
Silent Valley의 자생식물을 보호해야 한다고 주장했다.
가족의 결혼 기대와 달리 고등교육을 택했다.
evidence: later worked in Britain on a reference book
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 내용 불일치
재배 식물의 염색체에 관한 책을 작업한 곳은 영국이다.
[지문 근거] “later worked in Britain on a reference book”

reading.stem: Berry Basket Saturday에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

blocks.title: Berry Basket Saturday
lines: lead
Follow the short trail to the berry stalls and meet the growers. A jam maker will demonstrate how different fruit combinations affect the flavor.
sub
Each admission ticket includes one tasting spoon at no extra charge.
sub
The trail opens at eleven in the morning.
sub
Children under seven enter free with a paying adult.
sub
A grower leads the first walk from the red gate.
sub
The jam demonstration is repeated at three in the afternoon.

choices: 첫 번째 산책은 재배 농민이 빨간 문에서 인솔한다.
7세 미만 어린이는 유료 입장한 어른과 함께 무료로 들어간다.
evidence: one tasting spoon at no extra charge
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 안내문 내용 불일치
입장권에 시식용 숟가락이 포함되어 있어 따로 구매할 필요가 없다.
[지문 근거] “one tasting spoon at no extra charge”

reading.stem: After-Dark Light Trail에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

blocks.title: After-Dark Light Trail
lines: lead
An outdoor path links six works made with lamps and reflected light. Keep to the marked route so that other visitors can see the installations.
sub
The last visitors enter forty minutes before closing.
sub
The route is closed on Mondays.
sub
Printouts are unnecessary: a booking code on your phone is enough.
sub
Switch off your camera flash on the path.
sub
The route begins at the east gate and ends beside the lake.

evidence: last visitors enter forty minutes before closing
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 안내문 내용 일치
폐장 40분 전이 마지막 입장 시각이다.
[지문 근거] “last visitors enter forty minutes before closing”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [3점]
blocks: Two cafés are thinking about offering breakfast near a station. The owner of one announces ① <u>that</u> her doors will open at six next month. Whether the announcement discourages her rival ② <u>depend</u> on its credibility. A printed menu alone is unlikely ③ <u>to settle</u> the matter. A delivery van ④ <u>unloading</u> ovens before dawn sends a stronger signal because the expense is real. The rival must then decide whether entering the breakfast market is still worth ⑤ <u>doing</u> when another café has already paid to prepare for it.
evidence: Whether the announcement discourages her rival
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 어법
Whether로 시작하는 명사절 전체가 하나의 주어이므로 depends가 옳다. unloading은 delivery van을 꾸민다.
[지문 근거] “Whether the announcement discourages her rival”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3점]
blocks: Look at a plain ball under a ceiling lamp. Its upper surface appears ① <u>brighter</u> than its lower surface, so the change in shade helps an observer see its ② <u>curved</u> shape. Now imagine an animal with darker coloring on its back and lighter coloring underneath. When light falls from above, that arrangement can ③ <u>counteract</u> the usual shading. As a result, the difference in brightness across the body becomes more ④ <u>pronounced</u>, and the animal looks flatter. A predator relying on ordinary shadows may therefore find the animal harder to ⑤ <u>detect</u>.
evidence: the animal looks flatter
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임
명암 차이가 줄어들어 몸이 평평하게 보인다는 내용이다. pronounced(뚜렷한)를 subtle 또는 slight로 바꾸어야 한다.
[지문 근거] “the animal looks flatter”

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks: A listener hears a drum alternate with a bell for several minutes. Neither sound now attracts much attention. When the drummer strikes twice in a row, however, the listener looks up. In a different piece, consisting of drumbeats alone, the very same second strike goes unnoticed. Nothing about the sound itself explains the contrast. What matters is its <blank/> within the pattern the listener has learned. The extra drumbeat attracts attention precisely because the listener had prepared for a bell in its place. Surprise tells the listener that the previous rule may need revision.
evidence: the listener had prepared for a bell in its place
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 빈칸 추론
같은 북소리라도 예상한 순서를 깨면 두드러진다. 소리의 물리적 성질이 아니라 학습한 패턴에서 예측 가능한지가 관건이다. 근거 표현은 “the listener had prepared for a bell in its place”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks: Two banks serve different towns and have never lent each other money. When one closes, customers at the other begin forming a line outside its doors. Some privately believe their bank is healthy, yet fear that other customers will empty its available cash. They withdraw before their neighbors do. Soon the bank cannot supply notes quickly enough, and the line gets longer still. Trouble has crossed the boundary without a loan crossing it. In this case, people acting to avoid a shortage help produce it, showing how <blank/>.
choices: a bank's closure proves that its neighbors are equally weak
customers become safer when everyone waits for everyone else
shared investments are necessary for a shortage to spread
expectations can transmit a crisis without a direct financial link
a loan always transfers an equal risk to both towns
evidence: people acting to avoid a shortage help produce it
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 빈칸 추론
서로 대출하지 않았는데도 타인의 인출을 우려해 돈을 찾는 행동이 실제 부족을 만들었다. 기대 자체가 위기를 전파한 것이다. 근거 표현은 “people acting to avoid a shortage help produce it”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3점]
blocks: A child easily puts four buttons into a jar but hesitates when asked to place minus four buttons beside them. At a shop counter the same child understands perfectly that a customer still owes four coins. A bank statement may print that amount in red, and a lift may label a level below the street B1. Neither practice changes the arithmetic; it changes how the reader meets it. The sign that looks strange on its own becomes manageable when a familiar situation carries the idea of being below a reference point. Such devices allow us to <blank/>.
choices: show that negative amounts have no practical use
avoid choosing a reference level altogether
convert every debt into a physical object
handle negative quantities through everyday conventions
replace subtraction with a count of visible objects
evidence: a familiar situation carries the idea of being below a reference point
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 빈칸 추론
빚, 빨간 인쇄, 지하층 표시는 음수를 없애지 않고 익숙한 상황과 표기로 풀어 준다. 근거 표현은 “a familiar situation carries the idea of being below a reference point”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3점]
blocks: A survey finds that students who cycle to class report more energy. It would be tempting to advise every tired student to buy a bicycle. But the cyclists may live nearer the school, sleep longer, or belong to families with different schedules. A larger survey would estimate the association more precisely while leaving all three alternatives open. To decide what difference cycling itself makes, a researcher needs a comparison in which <blank/>. Otherwise the journey and the conditions that make that journey possible change together.
choices: factors other than the mode of travel are kept comparable across groups
the description of energy is replaced with a longer question
the original group is surveyed more often than the rest
distance and sleeping time vary together even more strongly
students choose whatever condition makes them most energetic
evidence: the journey and the conditions that make that journey possible change together
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 빈칸 추론
통학 방법과 수면·거리 등이 함께 달라지므로 자전거 자체의 효과를 보려면 다른 조건이 유사해야 한다. 근거 표현은 “the journey and the conditions that make that journey possible change together”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
blocks: Envy is often difficult to detect even in one's own account of a quarrel. ① A performer passed over for a leading role may dislike admitting that a friend's success has hurt. ② She can more comfortably tell herself that the selection process was unfair. ③ A theater usually announces the names of its leading performers in larger print than those of the supporting cast. ④ Then her anger feels like a defense of justice, and she stops examining the painful comparison that started it. ⑤ The emotion stays hidden because an acceptable explanation has taken the place of an uncomfortable one.
evidence: an acceptable explanation has taken the place of an uncomfortable one
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 흐름과 무관한 문장
다른 문장들은 질투가 공정성에 대한 분노로 위장되는 과정을 보여 준다. 출연자 이름의 인쇄 크기는 이 심리 과정과 관계가 없다. 근거 표현은 “an acceptable explanation has taken the place of an uncomfortable one”이다.

reading.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: Suppose a newspaper reported the winner of a school debate twenty years ago. Anyone standing in the hall at the time could have learned the winner's name.
Her concern is its continuing prominence. A reader searching for her present work must first pass through a record of an event that ceased to matter to her long ago.
Now a search for that person's name instantly produces the old report. She does not claim that the public announcement was a secret or that the paper originally obtained it in an improper way.
This concern illustrates a distinction. Keeping private facts from being revealed and asking that an old public fact become harder to find address different moments in the life of information.
evidence: Her concern is its continuing prominence
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 글의 순서 (2점)
(B) - (A) - (C)의 순서이다. 당시 공개된 이름의 수집 자체에는 이의가 없음을 설명한 뒤, 지금도 앞에 표시되는 것이 문제임을 밝히고 두 요구를 구분한다.
[지문 근거] “Her concern is its continuing prominence”

reading.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
blocks: At the beginning of the year, a worker cycled to work every morning. By autumn she was taking the underground, and a friend concluded that she had lost her taste for cycling.
The new route took twice as long by bicycle, while a newly opened station had shortened the train journey. She still went on long weekend rides whenever she had time.
The commute can therefore be explained without inventing a new dislike. To infer a change in preferences, it helps first to ask whether the costs of acting on the old ones have changed.
The friend had noticed a change in behavior, but he knew little about the alternatives available to her. In July her office had moved from a nearby street to the other side of a hill.
evidence: The new route
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 글의 순서 (3점)
(C) - (A) - (B)의 순서이다. 친구가 모르는 사무실 이전을 먼저 밝히고 새 경로의 비용을 비교한 뒤, 기호 변화 없이도 행동 변화를 설명할 수 있다고 결론짓는다.
[지문 근거] “The new route”

reading.stem: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
blocks: For avoidance to work, the animal needs some recognizable feature to link the earlier meal to this plant.

A grazing animal samples a leaf and later becomes ill. ( ① ) On another visit it passes the same plant without taking a bite. ( ② ) A particular bitter taste can supply such a link. Once associated with illness, it can discourage another mouthful before much is eaten. ( ③ ) This does not mean every plant with a bitter taste will make the animal ill. ( ④ ) Nor does it mean the animal has worked out a chemical account of what happened inside its stomach. ( ⑤ ) The useful outcome is a practical one: an experience from yesterday can change what goes into today's meal.
evidence: A particular bitter taste can supply such a link
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 문장 삽입 (2점)

reading.stem: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3점]
blocks: That movement of the ground is far harder to notice than a rising line of water on a pier.

A class drawing the effects of the Moon on Earth showed two bulges in the oceans and a perfectly rigid globe beneath them. ( ① ) Their teacher first accepted the drawing as a way to compare sea levels at different points. ( ② ) Then she reminded the class that the Moon's pull acts on material in the solid Earth as well as on seawater. ( ③ ) Even a station fixed to the ground can undergo a small change in position as the pattern of attraction changes. ( ④ ) The difference in visibility helps explain why the pupils had included the ocean's response but left the land's response out of every drawing. ( ⑤ ) Their revised diagrams showed both responses, with a note that the displacement of the solid surface was greatly exaggerated.
evidence: The difference in visibility

reading.stem: 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: In a classroom simulation, participants selected a partner for a paid task. The partner profiles gave no information about skill or reliability. Each displayed only a name, and one name happened to sound more familiar to each participant. Some students accepted a smaller payment to work with the person whose name resembled those in their neighborhood. They had obtained no evidence about either partner's ability. Nevertheless, a guess about who was similar to them had reduced what they would earn before the task even began.
An (A) impression of similarity can impose an economic (B) on the person acting on it.
evidence: no evidence about either partner's ability
reduced what they would earn

41-42.head: [41~42] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
blocks: A visitor to a design exhibition selected a blue mug and explained that its handle was visibly wider than the other mug's. Afterwards the organizer showed her a photograph: the two mugs offered to her had (a) <u>identical</u> handles. Only one had been displayed beside a sign in her favorite color. The photograph did not prove that the sign had guided her choice. It did, however, give a reason to (b) <u>question</u> her first explanation. When asked why we act, we can usually produce an answer before we have considered what evidence would distinguish it from a rival account. The ease with which a reason comes to mind can (c) <u>verify</u> its truth; the visitor's explanation sounded entirely reasonable and was nevertheless inconsistent with the photograph. We ought to treat such accounts as (d) <u>proposals</u> to investigate. A good investigator asks what observation might (e) <u>challenge</u> the story, especially when its author is the person who made the choice.

43-45.head: [43~45] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
blocks: During the school's practice relay, Rosa ran the first turn so fast that her partner had to reach backwards for the baton. It fell. The loudest sound Rosa heard afterwards was the hollow tap of metal on the track. That evening (a) <u>she</u> went back to find the exact place it had landed.

A chalk mark showed where the younger runner had expected to receive it. Rosa compared that mark with (b) <u>her</u> own hurried footprint. The marks were two strides apart. She invited the younger runner to practise starting at the chalk line the next day.

On race day the hand appeared just as Rosa counted four. The baton left (c) <u>her</u> fingers smoothly. When a reporter praised Rosa's speed, (d) <u>she</u> pointed to the chalk line fading beside the track and asked him to photograph both runners there.

At the practice, the younger runner tied a strip of red cloth to (e) <u>her</u> wrist. Rosa could now see the waiting hand without turning her head. After several exchanges the two agreed to take the cloth off and trust the rhythm of their steps.
